score_notes.retention: The first line is 12 words and 'And you're fine' lands at 3.5 s. Two trackers move in the hook: the BODY readout from 0:04 and the DepthMeter from 0:31, with the route and the red 'wall' tick shown at 0:28. The one-way rule (0:16) and the borrowed-fix promise ending 'until there isn't one' (0:44) are both in the rules. The first turn is 'Easy. Except' at 1:34 (21%). A numbered problem ladder leads into a T4 rug pull at 2:41 (36%), where the readout that has been falling since the ferry turns out to be the killer. The midpoint re-hook comes at 4:00 (54%), after the sperm whale threat. The low point (starving, remora quiet) is at 67%, the wall at 78%, a real decision at 5:57, the floor at 85%, and the hunger loop pays as both food and threat before the plastic reveal. Measured numbers: 49% second-person sentences, 12 you-words in the first 30 s, 3.5 pivots/min, 7.6 numbers/min, 178 wpm. Remaining risk: a familiar premise (PLAYBOOK §10C), and the remora is a fictional companion that some viewers will nitpick.
score_notes.reference: Every alignment row now describes a device that is actually in the VO, with reference timestamps re-checked against research/corpus/whatif/*.md: the one-way rule (_lu85gSD39k @0:07 -> our 0:16 -> stranding at the end, BILLION-YEARS @11:46-11:50), the mute companion readout that turns tender (@0:24-0:29 -> @11:43), the 'everyone... but you' narrowing (6oZ9fdM0n50 @0:10-0:15), the numbered problem ladder (y300HjYnHPw @2:41-3:49), and the climax decision that spends a planted number (y300HjYnHPw @7:05-7:11). The upgrade-4 hand-wave is gone: 8,200 m is the wall, and the last 2,700 m costs the way back. Stamp gaps are reported as measured (33-70 s), not claimed to be in range. Held at 8, not 9, because there is no second spoken voice; the remora is mute by design for a single Kokoro voice.
score_notes.originality: The originality gate passes. The highest 5-gram share is 0.08%, with research/corpus/whatif/PLAYBOOK.md, from beat-name phrases, and there is no shared 8-word run. Fact fixes: giant squid replaces colossal squid; the tuna exchanger sits between the gills and the body (the heart runs cold); 'man-made fibres' replaces 'plastic fibres'; 253 m is worded as 'the deepest anyone has dived on a single breath', not an official record; ears and sinuses flood as a stated consequence; 'Your gills are fine'; the heat drain is blood-flow-limited (x30 at the surface, x100 at 4 C) and runs from the ferry onward; TMAO is described as 'as concentrated as the sea', not 'saltier'; the geography is fixed (fall near Guam, trench a few hundred km SW, snailfish cousin 'one trench north'). The title is changed away from the competitors' exact title. Speculation is flagged out loud at 5:54 ('this is our guess') and on screen.
score_notes.producibility: New assets are cut from about 28 to 4 components (whatif/Hud, Ferry, GillDiagram, Fish) plus 1 kit edit (DepthMeter marks). Everything else is kit figures, core layers or inline SVG strings in the generator. Snow, rays and tints are done with crossfaded layers or the depth track; the giant squid and amphipods are kit stand-ins; the chamber, bathtub and jar are core layers. The HUD is a generator rule with a per-scene state table, and the timings are Kokoro measurements from the Spark. The storyboard validates (80 scenes, 443.9 s). Every shot is under 15 s (longest 13.8 s), and the 10-second gate shot is named. Held at 7 because kits/whatif/ still doesn't exist, the four components and the DepthMeter marks edit are unbuilt, and caption word timings are estimates until the real TTS render.
